name: Pokolbin

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, hot summer

climate: Few classic table-wine grapes keep their freshness in heat like this. It suits fortified wine, table grapes and raisins.
Syrah is at its warm limit. It can ripen too fast, giving heavy, soft wine that has lost its freshness.
Chardonnay is at its warm limit. It can ripen too fast, giving heavy, soft wine that has lost its freshness.
Sémillon is at its warm limit. It can ripen too fast, giving heavy, soft wine that has lost its freshness.
Most rain falls while the vines grow. Damp leaves invite mildew and rot, so growers spray more and pick carefully.

soil.rock: Sandstone is sand bound into rock. It weathers to light, sandy soil that drains freely. Shale and mudstone are fine-grained rocks that hold heat well and are moderately fertile.
soil.top: The topsoil stores water through dry spells, but stays wet and cold after rain, which slows ripening and can swell the grapes. Its pH is close to neutral, so vines take up the nutrients they need easily.

land: Gentle slopes. Enough tilt to drain cold air and rain away, which lowers frost risk, yet still easy to farm by machine.

winkler: Best for big crops of everyday wine, or table grapes.
